Makala hii inachanganua nomino ambatani za Kiswahili zinazokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano.
Kanuni hii huonesha utaratibu wa kujenga neno kamili kwa kutumia vijenzi.
Mabano katika kanuni hii hudhihirisha mipaka na hufutwa kuashiria kuwa sheria za uundaji wa maneno hazina ufikiaji wa muundo wa maneno yaliyotokana na ngazi za awali.
Utafiti huu ulifanywa baada ya kubaini kuwa baadhi ya nomino ambatani za Kiswahili hukiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano hasa pale ambapo mabadiliko hutokea katikati mwa neno baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa.
Nomino ambatani ifuatayo inadhihirisha mabadiliko yanayotokea katikati mwa neno baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa; [mw [enyekiti]] → [we [enyeviti]].
Katika utafiti huu tulikusanya data kutoka kwenye Kamusi Kuu ya Kiswahili (2015) ambapo nomino ambatani thelathini zinazokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano zilitumika kama data ya msingi.
Nomino hizi zilichaguliwa kwa kuzingatia sifa bainifu za ukiukaji wa Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano (KKM).
Utafiti huu uliongozwa na mhimili mmoja wa nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia iliyoasisiwa na Kiparsky (1982) na kuendelezwa na Katamba na Stonham (2019): Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano.
Nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia iliibuka kufidia mtazamo wa Chomsky wa Sarufi Zalishi ambao haukutambua kiwango cha mofolojia kama kiwango mahususi cha lugha.
Kimsingi nadharia hii inaonesha uhusiano wa sheria zinazojenga maumbo ya kimofolojia na sheria zinazodhibiti namna maumbo hayo yanavyotamkwa.
Data iliyohusiana na mada ya utafiti ilikusanywa maktabani.
Baadhi ya makala ambazo zilitumika katika utafiti huu ni tasnifu za awali, makala ya mtandaoni na majarida.
Utafiti huu uliongozwa na usampulishaji kimakusudi ili kufikia maneno husika ya nomino ambatani yaliyo na sifa bainifu.
Matokeo ya utafiti huu yaliwasilishwa kwa njia ya michoro, majedwali na maelezo.
Utafiti huu unachangia isimu hasa kupitia kuelewa na kueleza mbinu za mwambatano katika lugha ya Kiswahili,

maana ya maneno, toponimu, eponimu na mwambatano (Rubanza, 1996; Buberwa, 2011; Matinde, 2012).
Mada ya makala hii inapatikana katika eneo jumla la mofolojia.
Huu ni utanzu wa isimu unaoshughulikia muundo wa maneno (Habwe na Karanja, 2004).
Haspelmath na Sims (2013) wanaeleza mofolojia kama utanzu wa isimu unaochunguza muundo wa ndani wa maneno.
Kutokana na fasili hizi tunakubaliana na mawazo ya wataalam hawa kuwa mofolojia ni tawi la isimu ambalo hujihusisha na muundo wa maneno.
Mofolojia kama taaluma imegawanywa katika matawi mawili makuu: mofolojia ya minyambuliko ya maneno na mofolojia ya uundaji wa maneno.
Mofolojia ya minyambuliko ya maneno hushughulika na mchakato wa minyambuliko ya maneno ambayo huwekwa kwenye mizizi ya maneno kuwakilisha maana mbalimbali lakini minyambuliko hiyo haibadili aina ya neno hilo.
Mofolojia ya uundaji wa maneno ni eneo ambalo hushughulikia mikondo na matokeo ya kiisimu ya uundaji wa maneno kwa kuweka viambishi katika mizizi ya maneno, na kiambishi nyambuaji huunda neno jipya (Mgullu, 1999; Katamba & Stonham, 2019).
Uundaji wa maneno katika Kiswahili hufanyika kwa kutumia mbinu mbalimbali.
Mbinu hizi huwa na utaratibu maalumu wa kuzalisha maumbo yenye sifa tofauti.
Mbinu hizo ni kama; utohozi, ufupishaji (akronimu, uhulutishaji na mkato), upanuzi wa
Mbinu ya mwambatano hutumia maneno kamili yaliyoundwa kwa kutumia njia mbalimbali kama malighafi ya kuunda maneno mengine mapya kabisa.
Maumbo yanayozalishwa huandikwa kwa kuunganisha maneno mawili, kwa kutumia vistari au kuacha nafasi kati ya maneno yaliyoambatanishwa (Gichuru, 2010).
Hata hivyo, katika makala hii tuliamua kuandika nomino ambatani hizi katika namna mbili yaani; kuunganisha maneno yote na kutenganisha baadhi ya maneno katika nomino ambatani hizi ili kurahisisha uchanganuzi wa data uliofanyika.
Mgullu (1999) anatazama nomino ambatani kama mofu changamano.
Anasema kuwa mofu changamano ni mofu ambazo huundwa kwa kuweka pamoja angalau mashina au mizizi miwili ya maneno ambayo katika mazingira mengine mashina hayo yanaweza kutenganishwa na kila moja likawa ni neno kamili.
Maoni ya Mgullu (keshatajwa) yanayooana na yale ya Mustafa (2020) ambaye anashikilia huwa nomino ambatani, ni nomino zilizoundwa kwa kuunganisha maneno mawili (mizizi, kiini, mofimu huru au viambatisho vya leksia).
Maneno mawili haya huweza kuwa na nafasi, bila nafasi au kistariungio.
Mathalan kama inavyodhihirika katika nomino ambatani ‘mwanamke’ na ‘mwalimu mkuu.’

Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano ni mhimili ambao hutumiwa kuonesha utaratibu wa kujenga neno kamili kwa kutumia vijenzi vyake.
Mabano katika kanuni hii, huashiria mipaka ya vipashio mbalimbali na hufutwa kuonesha kuwa sheria za uundaji wa maneno hazina ufikiaji wa muundo wa maneno yaliyotokana na ngazi za awali (Katamba & Stonham, 2019).
Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano huwa na mkabala ambao unasisitiza kuwa mabano ya katikati huwa ya kwanza kufutwa katika kiwango cha leksia.
Kutokana na matokeo ya mkabala huu, maneno yanayoingiliana katikati mwa ngazi leksia hayawezi kuathiriwa na sheria za fonolojia mzunguko (Kiparsky, 1982; Katamba na Stonham, 2019).
Neno ambatani kama hili lililo hapo juu linapoundwa na kufikia hatua ya 3 linakuwa na mofimu mbili tu, yaani {mw} + {anamke} kinyume na ilivyokuwa katika hatua ya 1 ambapo lilikuwa na mofimu {{mw}kia.

Kwa mujibu wa Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano, katika hatua ya 3 huwezi kutenga {ana} na {mke} na hivyo basi hakuna mabadiliko yanayostahili kutokea katika mofimu hii.
Katika wingi, nomino ambatani mwanawake inakuwa wanawake ilhali tunajua kuwa katika umoja tuna mofimu mbili {mw} na {anamke}, mabadiliko haya katikati mwa mofimu {anamke} baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa huwa ni jambo la kushangaza kwani Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano hairuhusu mabadiliko kutokea katikati mwa neno baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa.
Baadhi ya nomino ambatani za Kiswahili hukiuka utaratibu huu na hili ndilo tatizo linalotafitiwa.
Baada ya kufuta mabano, maneno yanayotokana na mofolojia na sheria za uundaji wa maneno hazina ufikiaji wa muundo wa ndani wa maneno.
Mkabala huu unaruhusu urejeleaji wa nje wala si ndani ya neno baada ya mabano kufutwa.
Mofimu ya kwanza katika neno zima huweza kuwekwa katika hali ya wingi bila kuingia katika mofimu ya pili katika neno zima (Allen, 1978; Siegel, 1974).
Mofimu ya kwanza tunayorejelea hapa ni kiambishi cha ngeli kinachopatikana katika neno la kwanza la nomino ambatani, na mofimu ya pili ikiwa ni sehemu ya nomino ambatani inayobeba mzizi au shina la neno la kwanza pamoja na neno la pili au tatu katika neno ambatani, mathalan nomino ambatani ‘mwanamke’ ina mofimu mbili ambazo ni {mw} ikiwa mofu ya kwanza na mofimu ya pili {anamke).

Tafiti za Awali
Katikiro (2018) alitafiti kuhusu tathmini ya maana katika maneno ambatani ya Kiswahili.
Katika utafiti huo alishughulikia ubainishaji wa mchango wa maana za manenojenzi katika maana tokeo ya neno ambatani.
Akirejelea Gordian (2010), alidai kuwa maneno ambatani hutokana na mchakato wa kimofolojia wa kuambatisha maneno mawili yaliyo tofauti kimaana na kiumbo ili kuunda neno moja jipya lenye maana moja au lenye kurejelea kitu au dhana moja.
Katika utafiti huu, Katikiro (2018) alijikita katika uchunguzi wa tawi la semantiki ambalo hujihusisha na maana katika tungo tofauti ambazo ni kinyume na utafiti tuliotekeleza ambao ulijihusisha na tawi la isimu la mofolojia.
Hata hivyo, maarifa kutoka utafiti huu yalitufaa katika kufahamu mchakato wa kimofolojia wa uundaji nomino ambatani kwa kuambatisha maneno mawili yaliyo tofauti kimaana na kiumbo ili kuunda dhana moja.
Usomaji mpana wa makala maktabani, vitabu, na makala ya mtandao ulinuiwa kupata taarifa muhimu kuhusu ukiukaji wa KKM ya Mofolojia Leksia katika uundaji wa nomino ambatani za Kiswahili na pia kuelewa mbinu ya mwambatano katika lugha ya Kiswahili.
Maelezo yaliyopatikana yalikuwa na mashiko katika kubainisha pengo linaloshughulikiwa na utafiti huu.
Gituru (2019) katika utafiti wake juu ya unyambulishaji wa vitenzi katika Kigĩchũgũ, alibaini mifanyiko na mfuatano wa vitenzi vya Kigĩchũgũ katika mchakato wa unyambuzi kwa kuongozwa na nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia na Kanuni ya Kioo.
Aidha katika uchunguzi huu alidhihirisha kuwa Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano huonesha mageuzi ya vitenzi yanayotokea katika mchakato wa unyambuzi, na maumbo mbalimbali huungana kuwa kitenzi kimoja.
Utafiti huu ulikuwa msingi wa kueleza utaratibu wa Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano katika mchakato wa uundaji maneno na maelezo zaidi kuhusu nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia.
Buberwa (2017) akichunguza ruwaza za kimofolojia za majina ya mahali katika lugha ya Kihaya, alitambua mpangilio wa vipashio vinavyounda majina hayo na kuonesha jinsi vipashio vilipangana kimsonge kwa kuongozwa na mhimili wa Kanuni ya Ngazi Leksia ya Mofolojia Leksia.
Katika utafiti huo alieleza nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia kwa uwazi.
Hata hivyo, tofauti kuu kati ya utafiti wa Buberwa (2017) na utafiti huu ni kuwa utafiti wake ulichunguza mpangilio wa maneno ya Kihaya na kuonesha jinsi vipashio vinapangwa kimsonge kwa kuongozwa na mhimili wa Kanuni ya Ngazi Leksia ya Mofolojia Leksia.
Kwa upande mwingine, utafiti tuliotekeleza ulichunguza nomino ambatani za Kiswahili zinazokiuka KKM ya Mofolojia Leksia.
Utafiti huu ulitufaa katika kueleza dhana ya nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia.
Odden (2019) katika uchunguzi wake kuhusu kutabiri toni katika Kikuria, alitambua kuwa Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano hukiukwa katika uwekaji wa toni katika vitenzi vya Kikuria hasa sheria ya kuhamishwa kwa shina inapokuwa wazi kwa mabano ya ndani ya shina.
Anaendelea kusema kuwa hali hii hutokea wakati toni huhamishwa kutoka kiambishi kwenda shina la kitenzi cha Kikuria na hivyo basi, hukiuka KKM ambayo hairuhusu fonolojia kurejelea mofolojia ya ndani ya neno.

Maarifa kutoka utafiti huu yalitusaidia katika kuelewa dhana ya mwambatano ambayo utafiti tuliotekeleza ulichunguza.
Kiparsky (1982) alieleza kuhusu mkabala wa kufuta mabano ambao unasisitiza kwamba mabano ya katikati huwa ya kwanza kufutwa katika kiwango cha leksia.
Kama matokeo ya mkabala huu, maneno yanayoingiliana katikati mwa ngazi leksia hayawezi kuathiriwa na sheria za fonolojia mzunguko.
Baada ya kufuta mabano, maneno yanayotokana na mofolojia huchukuliwa kana kwamba yalibuniwa.
Kwa maoni ya Kiparsky (1982), utasa huu unaenea kwa michakato ya mofolojia na sheria za uundaji wa maneno hazina ufikiaji wa muundo wa ndani wa maneno yaliyotokana na kiwango cha awali.
Maarifa haya yalifaa katika utafiti uliotekelezwa.
Gichuru (2010), akichunguza nomino ambatani za Kiswahili, alibainisha na kuainisha taratibu pamoja na kanuni zinazohusika katika uundaji wa nomino ambatani kwa kuongozwa na mihimili sita ya nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia.
Utafiti wake ulidondoa data yake kutoka Nyuso za Mwanamke (2010), Kamusi ya Isimu na Falsafa ya Lugha (2004) na Kamusi ya Kiswahili Sanifu (2004).
Utafiti huo ulitilia mkazo maumbo ya nomino ambatani, kanuni na taratibu zilizohusika katika kuunda nomino ambatani na uhusiano wa kisarufi uliopo baina ya vijenzi vya nomino ambatani.
Ni ukweli kwamba utafiti wa Gichuru (2010) ulikuwa na mshabaha kiasi na utafiti tuliotekeleza kwani tafiti zote zilijikita katika aina moja ya data ambayo ni nomino ambatani na nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia.
Akitafiti kuhusu kuondoa mzunguko kama chanzo cha ugumu wa fonolojia, Cole (1995) alitambua mofolojia ya ndani ya neno kuwa wazi kwa fonolojia hata baada ya neno kuundwa kikamilifu.
Anaendelea kusema kuwa lazima muundo wa ndani wa mofolojia ya neno uonekane ili kupata athari za mzunguko kwa kuweka vizuizi katika vikoa vilivyoainishwa kimofolojia.
Kutokana na uchunguzi huu, tulipata maarifa jinsi mofolojia ya ndani huonekana kwa fonolojia, hali ambayo ni kinyume na Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano inayoruhusu fonolojia kurejelea muundo wa nje wa neno.
Hili lilitufaa kutambua jinsi baadhi za nomino ambatani za Kiswahili hukiuka KKM kwa kuruhusu fonolojia kuangalia muundo wa ndani wa nomino husika baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa.
Hata hivyo, tafiti hizi zina tofauti kwani Gichuru (2010) alijikita katika uchanganuzi wa uundaji wa nomino ambatani za Kiswahili na uambishaji wake kisarufi kwa kuongozwa na mihimili sita ya Mofolojia Leksia (Kanuni ya Mzunguko Kamili, Kanuni ya Ngazi Leksia, Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano, Kanuni ya Kuhifadhi Muundo, Kanuni ya Ufinyu wa Sifa na Kanuni ya Kwingineko ya Mofolojia Leksia) ilhali utafiti huu ulihusika na kuchunguza nomino ambatani zilizokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano kwa kuchukua mofimu za wingi kwa maneno yote yanayounda neno husika.
Maarifa kuhusu nomino ambatani na nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia kutoka kwa utafiti huu yalikuwa ya kufaa katika utafiti wa mada hii teule.
Mapitio haya ya maandishi yamedhihirisha kuwa ingawa kuna tafiti ambazo zimefanyika kuhusiana na mbinu ambatani ya kuunda nomino za Kiswahili, ukiukaji wa Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano haujawekwa bayana.
Kwa hivyo, makala hii inadhihirisha baadhi za nomino ambatani za Kiswahili zinazokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano hasa zinapokubali mabadiliko kutokea katikati mwa neno baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa.
Misingi ya Nadharia
Orgun na Inkelas (2002) walieleza kuwepo kwa sababu za kutazama tena ufutaji mabano.
Katika utafiti wao walieleza kuhusu ufutaji wa mabano ambapo waligundua kuwa ufutaji mabano haujapewa uzingativu mwingi katika mofolojia ya maneno.
Walidhihirisha kauli hii kwa kurejelea Pesetsky (1979) ambaye alieleza kuwa mkabala wa kufuta mabano unaruhusu fonolojia kurejelea mipaka iliyotolewa na ujenzi wa mofolojia wa nje, lakini hauruhusu urejeleaji wa muundo wa ndani ulioingia zaidi.
Maarifa ya Orgun na Inkelas (2002) yalifaa utafiti huu kwa kuwa yalikuwa ni kichocheo
Makala hii iliongozwa na nadharia ya Mofolojia Leksia (ML) iliyoasisiwa na Kiparsky (1982) na kuendelezwa na Katamba na Stonham (2019).

Procedure. This article analyzes Swahili compound nouns that violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule. This rule outlines the procedure for constructing a complete word using morphemes. Parentheses in this rule indicate boundaries and are deleted to signify that word formation rules do not access the structure of words formed at previous levels. This study was conducted after it was observed that some Swahili compound nouns violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule, especially when changes occur in the middle of the word after various morphemes are combined. The following compound noun illustrates the changes that happen in the middle of a word after various morphemes are joined: [mw [enyekiti]] → [we [enyeviti]]. In this study, we collected data from the Kamusi Kuu ya Kiswahili (2015), where thirty compound nouns that violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule were used as primary data. These nouns were selected based on the distinctive features of violating the Parenthesis Deletion Rule (PDR). This study was guided by one pillar of the Lexical Morphology theory established by Kiparsky (1982) and developed by Katamba and Stonham (2019): the Parenthesis Deletion Rule. The theory of Lexical Morphology emerged to compensate for Chomsky's Generative Grammar perspective, which did not recognize morphology as a distinct level of language. Essentially, this theory demonstrates the relationship between the rules that form morphological structures and the rules that govern how those structures are pronounced. The data related to the research topic was collected from the library. Some of the works used in this study include previous dissertations, online articles, and journals. This research was guided by purposive sampling to identify relevant compound nouns with distinctive features. The findings of this study were presented through charts, tables, and explanations. This research contributes to linguistics, particularly by understanding and explaining compounding strategies in the Swahili language. INTRODUCTION

This is a branch of linguistics that deals with the structure of words (Habwe and Karanja, 2004). Haspelmath and Sims (2013) define morphology as a branch of linguistics that examines the internal structure of words. Based on these definitions, we agree with these scholars' views that morphology is a branch of linguistics concerned with the structure of words. Morphology as a discipline is divided into two main branches: inflectional morphology and word formation morphology. Inflectional morphology deals with the process of inflection in words, where inflectional affixes are added to word roots to represent various meanings, but these inflections do not change the word class. Word formation morphology is the field that addresses the linguistic processes and outcomes of creating new words by adding affixes to word roots, where a derivational affix forms a new word (Mgullu, 1999; Katamba & Stonham, 2019). Word formation in Swahili takes place through various methods. These methods follow a specific procedure for generating forms with different characteristics. These methods include borrowing, abbreviation (acronyms, blending, and clipping), and extension.  
The compounding method uses complete words formed through various processes as raw material to create entirely new words. The resulting forms are written by joining two words together, using hyphens, or leaving a space between the combined words (Gichuru, 2010). However, in this article we decided to write these compound nouns in two ways; that is, by combining all the words and by separating some of the words in these compound nouns in order to simplify the analysis of the data conducted. Mgullu (1999) views compound nouns as complex morphemes. He states that complex morphemes are morphemes formed by joining together at least two stems or roots of words, which, in other contexts, these stems can be separated and each one can be a complete word. Mgullu’s views (already mentioned) are in agreement with those of Mustafa (2020), who maintains that compound nouns are nouns formed by joining two words (roots, stems, free morphemes, or lexical affixes). These two words may be joined with a space, without a space, or with a hyphen. For example, as evident in the compound nouns 'mwanamke' and 'mwalimu mkuu.' The Parenthesis Deletion Rule is a principle used to show the process of constructing a complete word using its morphemes. Parentheses in this rule indicate the boundaries of the various morphemes and are deleted to show that the word formation rules have no access to the structure of words formed at earlier levels (Katamba & Stonham, 2019). The Parenthesis Deletion Rule has an approach that emphasizes that inner parentheses are deleted first at the lexical level. As a result of this approach, words formed in the middle of the lexical level cannot be affected by cyclic phonological rules (Kiparsky, 1982; Katamba and Stonham, 2019). A compound word like the one above, when formed and reaches stage 3, consists of only two morphemes, namely {mw} + {anamke}, unlike in stage 1 where it had the morpheme {{mw}kia. {ana}root + {{m}tail.{ke}root}. According to the Parenthesis Deletion Rule, at stage 3 you cannot separate {ana} and {mke}, and therefore no further changes should occur in this morpheme. In the plural, the compound noun "mwanawake" becomes "wanawake," whereas we know that in the singular there are two morphemes, {mw} and {anamke}. This change within the morpheme {anamke} after the various morphemes have been combined is surprising, since the Parenthesis Deletion Rule does not permit changes to occur within the word after the various morphemes have been joined. Some Swahili compound nouns violate this procedure, and this is the issue being investigated. After deleting the parentheses, words formed through morphology and word formation rules do not allow access to the internal structure of the words. This approach allows for external but not internal reference to a word after the parentheses have been deleted. The first morpheme in the entire word can be placed in the plural form without affecting the second morpheme in the entire word (Allen, 1978; Siegel, 1974). The first morpheme referred to here is the noun class prefix found in the first word of the compound noun, while the second morpheme is that part of the compound noun which carries the root or stem of the first word together with the second or third word in the compound, for example, the compound noun 'mwanamke' consists of two morphemes: {mw} as the first morpheme and {anamke} as the second. Katikiro (2018) conducted research on the evaluation of meaning in Swahili compound words. In that study, he addressed the identification of the contribution of the meanings of constituent morphemes to the resultant meaning of the compound word. Referring to Gordian (2010), he asserted that compound words are formed through a morphological process of joining together two words that are different in meaning and form to create a new word with a single meaning or one that refers to a single entity or concept. In this study, Katikiro (2018) focused on the examination of the branch of semantics, which deals with meaning in different constructions, in contrast to the study we conducted, which was concerned with the branch of linguistics known as morphology. However, the knowledge gained from this study was useful to us in understanding the morphological process of forming compound nouns by joining together two words that are different in meaning and form to create a single concept. Extensive reading of articles in the library, books, and online articles was intended to obtain important information about the violation of the Parenthesis Deletion Rule of Lexical Morphology in the formation of Swahili compound nouns and also to understand the compounding method in the Swahili language. The information obtained was instrumental in identifying the gap addressed by this study. Gituru (2019), in his study on verb inflection in Kigĩchũgũ, identified the processes and sequences of Kigĩchũgũ verbs during inflection, guided by the theory of Lexical Morphology and the Mirror Principle. Additionally, in this investigation, he demonstrated that the Parenthesis Deletion Rule illustrates the changes that verbs undergo during inflection, with various forms combining into a single verb. This study formed the basis for explaining the procedure of the Parenthesis Deletion Rule in the word formation process and provided further explanations about the theory of Lexical Morphology. Buberwa (2017), in examining the morphological patterns of place names in the Haya language, identified the arrangement of morphemes that form these names and demonstrated how the morphemes are linearly ordered, guided by the principle of the Lexical Level Rule of Lexical Morphology. This study was useful to us in explaining the concept of Lexical Morphology theory. This principle adopts an approach that emphasizes that inner parentheses are deleted first at the lexical level, and if reference is made in a compound noun, such reference is only to the first morpheme (Allen, 1978; Kiparsky, 1982; Katamba and Stonham, 2019). To shed more light on the violation of the Parenthesis Deletion Rule, we will explain the process of forming the compound noun ‘mjamzito’ from Table 2 as a representative of the other 29 compound nouns listed above, as illustrated in Figure 1 below:

The plural marker should be placed on the first morpheme, that is, {m}, and not on the second morpheme {jamzito}. According to the Parenthesis Deletion Rule, the grammatical inflection of the compound noun in the plural should be ٭wajamzito, a noun that creates grammatical ambiguity. To avoid this grammatical ambiguity, this noun allows grammatical inflection on the second morpheme, that is, {jawazito}, a situation which causes a change to occur in the middle of the compound noun 'mjamzito' after the various morphemes have been combined, resulting in ‘wajawazito’. This situation occurs in all the compound nouns we listed in Table 2, that is, these nouns take the plural marker in the second morpheme of the compound noun. However, Orgun and Inkelas (2002) contend the emergence of a theory that exposes the internal morphology to phonology even after the word has been fully formed, namely the theory of Prosodic Form. What is evident in this procedure is that the first stage involves separating the various units using parentheses. For example, at this stage, the affixes in the compound noun ‘mjamzito’ are separated from the stem [[[m]prefix [ja]stem] and [[m]prefix.[zito]stem]]. In the second stage, the inner parentheses are deleted to show the components of the compound noun; [[mja]N [mzito]]V, and in the third stage, the compound noun is already joined; [mjamzito]N, and the parentheses are removed to demonstrate the end of the compound noun formation process. After removing the parentheses, the words formed by combining morphological segments are treated as if they have never been combined; thus, they are considered whole from the beginning. The Optimal Shape Theory holds that all morphological information is visible to phonology (Prince and Smolensky, 1993). This view aligns with that of Cole (1995), who argues that the internal structure of a word’s morphology must be visible in order to obtain cyclic effects by imposing restrictions within morphologically defined domains. The perspectives of Orgun and Inkelas (2002) and Cole (1995) differ from those of scholars such as Siegel (1974), Allen (1978), Pesetsky (1979), Kiparsky (1982), Mohanan (1986), Inkelas (1990), Booij (1997), and Katamba & Stonham (2019), who maintain that after parentheses are deleted in the process of word formation, the Bracket Erasure Rule allows phonology to refer to only the outermost boundaries set in morphological structure, but does not permit reference to internal forms. In this study, we have demonstrated some Swahili compound nouns that violate the Bracket Erasure Rule by allowing changes to occur in the second morpheme of the compound noun that we listed in Table 2, where they take plural markers. For example: in the compound noun morphemes ‘mkemwenza,’ the first morpheme [m] and the second morpheme [kemwenza] take the plural form as [wa[kewenza]]. According to Orgun and Inkelas (2002), when parentheses are deleted in the process of forming this compound noun, the Bracket Erasure Rule does not allow phonology to refer to internal forms, for instance, the second morpheme {jamzito}. The removal of primary stress in the initial word does not occur only in Swahili compound nouns but also in other languages such as Spanish. discourses.source_txt: Makala hii inachanganua nomino ambatani za Kiswahili zinazokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano. Kanuni hii huonesha utaratibu wa kujenga neno kamili kwa kutumia vijenzi. Mabano katika kanuni hii hudhihirisha mipaka na hufutwa kuashiria kuwa sheria za uundaji wa maneno hazina ufikiaji wa muundo wa maneno yaliyotokana na ngazi za awali.
discourses.translated_txt: This article analyzes Swahili compound nouns that violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule. This rule outlines the procedure for constructing a complete word using morphemes. Parentheses in this rule indicate boundaries and are deleted to signify that word formation rules do not access the structure of words formed at previous levels.

discourses.source_txt: Utafiti huu ulifanywa baada ya kubaini kuwa baadhi ya nomino ambatani za Kiswahili hukiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano hasa pale ambapo mabadiliko hutokea katikati mwa neno baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa. Nomino ambatani ifuatayo inadhihirisha mabadiliko yanayotokea katikati mwa neno baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa; [mw [enyekiti]] → [we [enyeviti]]. Katika utafiti huu tulikusanya data kutoka kwenye Kamusi Kuu ya Kiswahili (2015) ambapo nomino ambatani thelathini zinazokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano zilitumika kama data ya msingi.
discourses.translated_txt: This study was conducted after it was observed that some Swahili compound nouns violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule, especially when changes occur in the middle of the word after various morphemes are combined. The following compound noun illustrates the changes that happen in the middle of a word after various morphemes are joined: [mw [enyekiti]] → [we [enyeviti]]. In this study, we collected data from the Kamusi Kuu ya Kiswahili (2015), where thirty compound nouns that violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule were used as primary data.

discourses.source_txt: Nomino hizi zilichaguliwa kwa kuzingatia sifa bainifu za ukiukaji wa Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano (KKM).
discourses.translated_txt: These nouns were selected based on the distinctive features of violating the Parenthesis Deletion Rule (PDR).

discourses.translated_txt: This study was guided by one pillar of the Lexical Morphology theory established by Kiparsky (1982) and developed by Katamba and Stonham (2019): the Parenthesis Deletion Rule.

Essentially, this theory demonstrates the relationship between the rules that form morphological structures and the rules that govern how those structures are pronounced.

discourses.source_txt: Mada ya makala hii inapatikana katika eneo jumla la mofolojia. Huu ni utanzu wa isimu unaoshughulikia muundo wa maneno (Habwe na Karanja, 2004). Haspelmath na Sims (2013) wanaeleza mofolojia kama utanzu wa isimu unaochunguza muundo wa ndani wa maneno. Kutokana na fasili hizi tunakubaliana na mawazo ya wataalam hawa kuwa mofolojia ni tawi la isimu ambalo hujihusisha na muundo wa maneno.
discourses.translated_txt: The topic of this article falls within the general area of morphology. This is a branch of linguistics that deals with the structure of words (Habwe and Karanja, 2004). Haspelmath and Sims (2013) define morphology as a branch of linguistics that examines the internal structure of words. Based on these definitions, we agree with these scholars' views that morphology is a branch of linguistics concerned with the structure of words.

discourses.source_txt: Mofolojia kama taaluma imegawanywa katika matawi mawili makuu: mofolojia ya minyambuliko ya maneno na mofolojia ya uundaji wa maneno. Mofolojia ya minyambuliko ya maneno hushughulika na mchakato wa minyambuliko ya maneno ambayo huwekwa kwenye mizizi ya maneno kuwakilisha maana mbalimbali lakini minyambuliko hiyo haibadili aina ya neno hilo. Mofolojia ya uundaji wa maneno ni eneo ambalo hushughulikia mikondo na matokeo ya kiisimu ya uundaji wa maneno kwa kuweka viambishi katika mizizi ya maneno, na kiambishi nyambuaji huunda neno jipya (Mgullu, 1999; Katamba & Stonham, 2019). Uundaji wa maneno katika Kiswahili hufanyika kwa kutumia mbinu mbalimbali.
discourses.translated_txt: Morphology as a discipline is divided into two main branches: inflectional morphology and word formation morphology. Inflectional morphology deals with the process of inflection in words, where inflectional affixes are added to word roots to represent various meanings, but these inflections do not change the word class. Word formation morphology is the field that addresses the linguistic processes and outcomes of creating new words by adding affixes to word roots, where a derivational affix forms a new word (Mgullu, 1999; Katamba & Stonham, 2019). Word formation in Swahili takes place through various methods.

discourses.source_txt: Akitafiti kuhusu kuondoa mzunguko kama chanzo cha ugumu wa fonolojia, Cole (1995) alitambua mofolojia ya ndani ya neno kuwa wazi kwa fonolojia hata baada ya neno kuundwa kikamilifu. Anaendelea kusema kuwa lazima muundo wa ndani wa mofolojia ya neno uonekane ili kupata athari za mzunguko kwa kuweka vizuizi katika vikoa vilivyoainishwa kimofolojia. Kutokana na uchunguzi huu, tulipata maarifa jinsi mofolojia ya ndani huonekana kwa fonolojia, hali ambayo ni kinyume na Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano inayoruhusu fonolojia kurejelea muundo wa nje wa neno. Hili lilitufaa kutambua jinsi baadhi za nomino ambatani za Kiswahili hukiuka KKM kwa kuruhusu fonolojia kuangalia muundo wa ndani wa nomino husika baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa.
discourses.translated_txt: In his research on eliminating cyclicity as a source of phonological difficulty, Cole (1995) identified the internal morphology of the word as being accessible to phonology even after the word has been fully formed. He goes on to state that the internal morphological structure of the word must be visible in order to capture the effects of cyclicity by imposing constraints within domains that are morphologically defined. From this analysis, we gained insight into how internal morphology is reflected in phonology, a situation that contrasts with the Parenthesis Deletion Rule, which allows phonology to refer only to the external structure of the word. This helped us to recognize how some Swahili compound nouns violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule by permitting phonology to access the internal structure of the compound noun after various morphemes have been joined.

discourses.source_txt: Hata hivyo, tafiti hizi zina tofauti kwani Gichuru (2010) alijikita katika uchanganuzi wa uundaji wa nomino ambatani za Kiswahili na uambishaji wake kisarufi kwa kuongozwa na mihimili sita ya Mofolojia Leksia (Kanuni ya Mzunguko Kamili, Kanuni ya Ngazi Leksia, Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano, Kanuni ya Kuhifadhi Muundo, Kanuni ya Ufinyu wa Sifa na Kanuni ya Kwingineko ya Mofolojia Leksia) ilhali utafiti huu ulihusika na kuchunguza nomino ambatani zilizokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano kwa kuchukua mofimu za wingi kwa maneno yote yanayounda neno husika.
discourses.translated_txt: However, these studies differ in that Gichuru (2010) focused on analyzing the formation of Swahili compound nouns and their grammatical inflection, guided by the six principles of Lexical Morphology (the Strict Cycle Principle, the Lexical Level Principle, the Parenthesis Deletion Rule, the Structure Preservation Principle, the Feature Minimality Principle, and the Elsewhere Condition of Lexical Morphology), whereas this study was concerned with examining compound nouns that violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule by taking plural morphemes for all the words that form the respective compound noun.

This article addresses Swahili compound nouns that violate the Parenthesis Deletion Rule by allowing changes to occur in the middle of the word after the various morphemes have been combined. The Optimal Shape Theory holds that all morphological information is visible to phonology (Prince and Smolensky, 1993). This view aligns with that of Cole (1995), who argues that the internal structure of a word’s morphology must be visible in order to obtain cyclic effects by imposing restrictions within morphologically defined domains. The perspectives of Orgun and Inkelas (2002) and Cole (1995) differ from those of scholars such as Siegel (1974), Allen (1978), Pesetsky (1979), Kiparsky (1982), Mohanan (1986), Inkelas (1990), Booij (1997), and Katamba & Stonham (2019), who maintain that after parentheses are deleted in the process of word formation, the Bracket Erasure Rule allows phonology to refer to only the outermost boundaries set in morphological structure, but does not permit reference to internal forms. In this study, we have demonstrated some Swahili compound nouns that violate the Bracket Erasure Rule by allowing changes to occur in the second morpheme of the compound noun that we listed in Table 2, where they take plural markers. For example: in the compound noun morphemes ‘mkemwenza,’ the first morpheme [m] and the second morpheme [kemwenza] take the plural form as [wa[kewenza]]. According to Orgun and Inkelas (2002), when parentheses are deleted in the process of forming this compound noun, the Bracket Erasure Rule does not allow phonology to refer to internal forms, for instance, the second morpheme {jamzito}. discourses.translated_txt: In the second cycle, the inner brackets are deleted; according to the cycle rule, the removal of the primary stress from the noun ‘mkaza’ and the reassignment of the primary stress onto the noun ‘mjomba’ renders the primary stress in the noun ‘mkaza’ weak, thus the primary stress is removed and newly placed on the penultimate syllable of the noun ‘mjomba,’ resulting in ‘mkazamꞌjomba.’ Chomsky and Halle (1968) claim that when primary stress is assigned to a particular position in a word, other stresses in the same word become weak, as is evident in the compound noun ‘mkazamjomba.’ The removal of stress from the first word and its reassignment on the second word in the process of Cyclic Phonology demonstrates that there is no violation of the CCC (Constituent Structure Constraint), because the rule considers this as a single word, not two words as before.

discourses.translated_txt: Morphological patterns require that the internal structure of the stem be visible to the external morpheme. This situation, where the internal structure is apparent to the external morpheme, is observed in compound nouns in Swahili that violate the Bracketing Erasure Principle, particularly when the second morphemes take plural markers. For instance, we shall use the compound noun 'mwanamke' as a representative of the nouns listed in Table 3 to show how the internal structure becomes visible to the external morpheme. The compound noun 'mwanamke' consists of two morphemes: {mw} and {anamke}, and when this compound noun is grammatically pluralized, the first morpheme {mw} and the second morpheme {anamke} both take plural prefixes to become {w} and {anawake}. This situation demonstrates how the prefix {m} of the noun ‘mke’ in the second morpheme {anamke} becomes visible to the first morpheme {mw}, and this is the reason why the compound nouns in Table 3 violate the Bracketing Erasure Principle. discourses.source_txt: Makala hii imeshughulikia nomino ambatani za Kiswahili zinazokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano. Ili kufikia lengo la kudhihirisha nomino ambatani za Kiswahili zinazokiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano tuliongozwa na mhimili wa Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano kueleza utaratibu unaohusika katika uundaji wa nomino ambatani na namna ambavyo nomino ambatani hizi hukiuka utaratibu huu hasa pale zinapoambishwa kisarufi katika wingi, hali ambayo husababisha mabadiliko katikati mwa neno baada ya vipashio mbalimbali kuunganishwa na mabano kubomolewa. Makala hii kwa muhtasari imeshughulika na kueleza jinsi baadhi ya nomino ambatani za Kiswahili hukiuka Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano kwa kuchukua utaratibu huu [wingi + Y1] + [wingi + Yn] mathalan; mkazamwana → wakazawana ambao ni kinyume cha Kanuni ya Kufuta Mabano kwani kanuni hii hairuhusu aina ya urejeleaji nyuma baada ya mabano kufutwa, na iwapo kutakuwa na urejeleaji nyuma hufuata utaratibu huu [wingi + Y1] + [Yn] kama inavyojitokeza katika nomino ambata; mwanamgambo → wanamgambo. Mwisho tulibaini uondoaji wa shadda msingi kutoka neno la kwanza la nomino ambatani na uwekaji upya wa shadda ya msingi katika silabi ya pili kutoka mwisho wa nomino ambatani husika.
discourses.translated_txt: This article has addressed Swahili compound nouns that violate the Bracket Deletion Principle. In order to demonstrate the existence of Swahili compound nouns which contravene this principle, we were guided by the framework of the Bracket Deletion Principle to explain the process involved in the formation of compound nouns and the ways in which these compounds violate this process, especially when they are grammatically pluralized, a situation that leads to changes in the middle of the word after various morphemes are joined and the brackets are removed. In summary, this article has explained how some Swahili compound nouns violate the Bracket Deletion Principle by following the pattern [plural + Y1] + [plural + Yn], for example: mkazamwana → wakazawana, which is contrary to the principle since the rule does not allow this type of backward reference after the deletion of brackets. If backward reference does occur, it follows the pattern [plural + Y1] + [Yn], as is evident in the compound noun; mwanamgambo → wanamgambo. Lastly, we observed the removal of the basic gemination from the first part of the compound noun and the reapplication of the basic gemination on the penultimate syllable of the relevant compound noun.
